CDC Study Reveals Timing of Flu Isolation Ends When Contagiousness is Highest
item.description: A CDC-led study published in the American Journal of Epidemiology on September 10, 2026, reveals that most people with the flu stop isolating when they are still likely contagious, increasing the risk of spreading the virus. The research, which analyzed data from approximately 1,300 individuals across Missouri, New York, and Tennessee during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 flu seasons, found that people typically shed the most viral RNA from their nose a median of four days after symptoms begin. However, most individuals end their isolation around this time, despite CDC guidelines recommending isolation until symptoms improve for 24 hours. The study showed that only 5.5% of people isolate from the community for the full recommended period, and less than 1% isolate from household members for the entire duration. About 80% isolate from the community for some time (median of four days), but only 21% isolate from household members (median of two days). The CDC's guidance states that people can end

item.title: Fox News Hosts Criticize Jack Smith's 'No Kings' Shirt Amid Political Tensions
item.description: Fox News personalities, including host Harris Faulkner and conservative podcast host Ben Ferguson, criticized former special counsel Jack Smith for wearing a 'No Kings' shirt at a music festival. The shirt, featuring a slogan associated with protests against former President Donald Trump, became the focus of a segment on 'The Faulkner Focus.' Faulkner questioned Smith's timing, suggesting he had 'time' for the outing while dealing with his congressional testimony. Ferguson accused Smith of hypocrisy, claiming it was 'pretty rich' for someone who tried to 'overturn an election' to wear the shirt. Smith's investigation led to the August 2023 indictment of Trump over efforts to overturn the 2020 election. The segment also included discussions about progressive Democratic candidates in the upcoming midterms, with Ferguson claiming they advocate for abolishing ICE, implementing government-run healthcare, and joining the International Criminal Court. item.title: Rapper LUCKI Injured in ComplexCon Altercation as LAPD Investigates Attempted Murder
item.description: The incident occurred on Saturday, October 3, during the ComplexCon event in Los Angeles. According to reports from HotNewHipHop citing TMZ, LUCKI, a Chicago-based rapper, was reportedly injured during an altercation outside the event. The rapper was taking photos with fans when an unidentified individual allegedly struck him in the face, causing a laceration near his face and neck. Footage obtained by PEOPLE shows LUCKI returning to a vehicle with a visible wound. The Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) responded to the scene around 4:45 p.m. local time, confirming that four people sustained injuries consistent with stab wounds or lacerations. Two individuals were hospitalized, one sought treatment independently, and a fourth declined medical attention. Playboi Carti was reportedly nearby during the incident, though there is no evidence linking him to the altercation. item.title: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton Investigates Small Pediatric Practice Over Vaccine Policies
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate, has initiated a controversial investigation into a small central Texas pediatric practice, demanding a 28-item list of financial benefits received from vaccine manufacturers. The investigation, which has been described as 'chilling' by health experts, centers on a pediatrician who has treated children in her community for 20 years. Paxton's Consumer Protection Division sent a letter in December demanding 10 years of vaccine purchase records and the practice's vaccine policy, emphasizing that merely citing the CDC's recommended childhood schedule would not suffice. The letter also instructed the doctor to maintain confidentiality regarding the investigation, warning that disclosure could jeopardize the ongoing probe. The 28-item demand sought every 'reward, financial benefit, bonus, discount, return, rebate or other consideration' received from vaccine makers, including minor perks like a $40 batch of cookies fro

item.title: Karen Allen's Behind-the-Scenes Journey Crafting Marion Ravenwood in 'Raiders of the Lost Ark' (1981)
item.description: Karen Allen, at 28 years old, brought a fierce independence and collaborative spirit to her role as Marion Ravenwood in 'Raiders of the Lost Ark' (1981), actively shaping the character to break away from the traditional 'damsel in distress' trope. Recommended by directors John Landis and Rob Cohen, Allen secured the role after a brief 15-minute meeting and screen test in Los Angeles, even before Harrison Ford was confirmed as Indiana Jones. She worked closely with director Steven Spielberg to ensure Marion was portrayed as an equal partner rather than mere eye candy, altering scenes to maintain her character's self-reliant edge. Spielberg praised her instincts, noting she played Marion as someone who had 'survived a hundred bar fights.' Filming at Elstree Studios in England, Allen's first scene involved hitting Ford square in the jaw, a moment that defined her character's tough introduction. She resonated deeply with Marion's scene of out-drinking a giant Sherpa in a freezing, smoky ba

item.title: Supermarket Shopping Habits Correlate with Political Preferences in UK Poll
item.description: A recent poll conducted by More in Common has revealed distinct political preferences among shoppers across major British supermarkets. The findings indicate that Labour leads among shoppers at Tesco, Asda, Waitrose, and Aldi, reflecting the party's steady national polling lead. Aldi shoppers are particularly politically divided, showing strong support for Labour alongside notable backing for Rupert Lowe's Restore Britain party. In contrast, shoppers at Sainsbury's and M&S (Marks & Spencer) favor the Conservatives, while Reform UK holds the top spot among Lidl and Morrisons shoppers. The poll comes amid rumors of an early general election, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham announcing plans to reform the UK voting system if Labour wins the next election. The study highlights how consumer behavior in retail settings may correlate with political leanings, suggesting that supermarket choices could be indicative of broader political preferences. item.title: Republican Dissent Grows as Internal Party Concerns Mount Over Trump's Influence
item.description: President Donald Trump faces a growing midterm backlash within his own party, according to University of Virginia political analyst Larry Sabato. Speaking on 'Scott MacFarland Reports,' Sabato highlighted warning signs in MAGA-fied states that previously backed Trump, noting a critical mass of voters including Democrats, independents, and a significant slice of Republicans who seek to send a message to Trump and the Republican Congress. Sabato emphasized that this internal dissent is unusual, stating, 'You don't see that all that often.' He predicted a Democratic wave fueled by Republicans ready to rebuke Trump, suggesting the movement could be larger than anticipated. Sabato also pointed to shifting Republican spending decisions as evidence of internal party concerns, noting that outside GOP Senate funding is moving from North Carolina to Kansas—a race previously considered less competitive. item.title: PewDiePie's OpenAI Ban Highlights Flaws in AI Distillation Detection Systems
item.description: PewDiePie, the popular YouTuber, has been banned twice by OpenAI while developing Ajax, a 9-billion-parameter AI model fine-tuned from Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 9B. The model is designed to run locally within his self-hosted Odysseus workspace, handling tasks like web browsing, email management, and calendar coordination without cloud data transmission. PewDiePie linked his bans to attempts to distill reasoning tokens from OpenAI's models, which violates OpenAI's terms of service. The case is significant because it mirrors the practices US agencies accused Chinese AI labs of using, as outlined in a recent NSA, CISA, and FBI advisory. The advisory recommends that providers quietly degrade output quality for suspected distillers rather than banning accounts outright, but OpenAI chose to ban PewDiePie, making it a visible case. The controversy also touches on broader issues of AI ethics, including whether companies that train models on public data have the right to object when users attempt to d

item.title: Texas AG Ken Paxton's Campaign Ad Sparks Confusion Over Missing Child Flyer Depiction
item.description: A political advertisement for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate, has generated significant confusion and criticism after it depicted a scene where Paxton appears to be tearing down a missing child flyer. The ad, funded by Texas PAC, a super PAC backed by Senate Republican leadership, was aired nationally during the early window of NFL coverage on Fox, including during the Cowboys-Texans game in Texas media markets. The ad's narrator claims Paxton is 'relentless about protecting Texas children' before cutting to a scene showing someone tearing down a missing child flyer with the caption, 'When missing posters go up, Ken Paxton takes them down.' Critics, including Democratic strategist Conor Rogers and Houston-based writer Gwen Howerton, expressed confusion and sarcasm over the ad's wording, with Howerton quipping, 'Finally, a guy who is willing to get tough on those missing kids,' and Texas trial attorney Israel Medina sarcastically writing on s

item.title: 19th-Century Sideshow Performer Mademoiselle Zana, Known as the Bearded Russian Lady, Featured in Historical Photographs
item.description: The article discusses a historical photograph of Mademoiselle Zana, a 19th-century sideshow performer who was promoted as 'The Only Bearded Russian Lady.' She gained notoriety during the late 1800s by touring Europe and the United States in dime museums, circuses, and novelty exhibitions. The photograph in question is a carte-de-visite (CdV) portrait, a popular format in the 19th century, which was produced by photographers like Charles Eisenmann of New York, who specialized in sideshow portraits. During the Victorian era, performers with unusual physical characteristics, such as excessive hair growth (hirsutism or hypertrichosis), often found employment in the sideshow circuit. Managers of these exhibitions frequently exaggerated or fabricated the backgrounds of performers to create exotic narratives for Western audiences. In this case, Zana was presented as Russian, adding an element of foreign intrigue to her act. The article notes that modern medical understanding would classify he

item.title: Pardoned Jan. 6 Rioter's 'Crusader March' Turns Violent as Nazi Group Interrupts Event
item.description: On Sunday, a planned 'Crusader March' organized by pardoned January 6 Capitol rioter Jake Lang turned chaotic when a group of self-described Nazis interrupted the event near Chicago's Bridgeview, Illinois. The demonstration, which Lang promoted with a poster referencing 'Stop the Islamification of Chicago' and branding Bridgeview as an 'Islamic military base,' drew significant backlash from local officials and counter-protesters. Bridgeview Mayor Steven Landek (D-IL) condemned Lang's rhetoric, stating, 'There is no place for the bigotry and hate-filled rhetoric espoused by Mr. Lang in our community.' During the event, Lang and his supporters, who wore red armbands with crosses, were confronted by a small Nazi group led by Trevor Raein and Greg Conte. The Nazis, dressed in white shirts and holding a banner reading 'JAKE LANG IS A JEW,' repeatedly shouted 'Heil Hitler' and claimed to be protesting Lang's 'Zionist ops for more wars for Jews.' item.title: Amateur Detectorist Uncovers Largest Roman Coin Hoard from Emperor Hadrian's Reign in Germany
item.description: In a remarkable archaeological discovery, amateur metal detectorist Oliver Riedl unearthed a hoard of 934 Roman silver denarii in Wesseling, Germany, marking the largest collection of its kind from Emperor Hadrian's reign ever found in the country. The coins, buried in a ceramic pot lined with straw, were discovered after Riedl's metal detector continued to beep persistently following the initial find of 15 coins. Authorities from the LVR Office for the Preservation of Archaeological Monuments in the Rhineland were called to the site, where they recovered the entire cache, which now resides at the LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn. The hoard, dating from 148 B.C.E. to 125 C.E., includes coins minted during the reign of Emperor Hadrian (117-138 C.E.), making it the largest such collection from this period in Germany and the fifth-largest globally. item.title: Trump's Threat to Withhold Federal Funds from Democrats Sparks Expert Criticism
item.description: President Donald Trump made a controversial statement at a rally in Ohio on October 3, 2026, where he indicated he would be less inclined to approve federal funding requests from Democratic elected officials and would not assist Democratic Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton if she defeated her Republican opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy. Security expert Miles Taylor, who served as a senior Homeland Security official under the first Trump administration, analyzed Trump's remarks in a Substack post published on October 5, 2026. Taylor described Trump's warning as a 'thinly veiled threat' that demonstrated the president had reached a 'total desperation stage.' Taylor argued that Trump's comments represented a 'disgusting and blatantly unconstitutional weaponization of presidential power,' as he was using taxpayer funds as a 'carrot-and-stick' to influence voting behavior. item.title: Oklahoma House Committee Recommends Mild Discipline for Rep. Danny Williams Amid Sexual Harassment Claims
item.description: The Oklahoma House of Representatives' ethics committee has faced criticism for its handling of a sexual harassment case involving state Representative Danny Williams, a Republican from Seminole. After a two-day closed-door hearing, the bipartisan committee determined that Williams sexually harassed multiple women and urinated in a cup left on an assistant's desk, but opted not to recommend expulsion. Instead, the committee suggested a public reprimand, removal from committee assignments and leadership roles, loss of access to a legislative assistant, and a prohibition on one-on-one contact with staff. The committee also urged Williams to resign and complete sexual harassment training, though these measures are not enforceable. House Speaker Kyle Hilbert implemented some of the recommendations, including stripping Williams of his committee roles and moving his office, but acknowledged he could not force Williams to resign or complete the training. item.title: Republican Redistricting Strategy Faces Backlash as Latino Voter Shifts Against Trump
item.description: According to Axios, Republicans who based part of their redistricting strategy on Donald Trump's gains with Latino men are now facing a potential backfire in the 2026 midterms. The shift in Latino voter preference, which previously helped Trump win the 2024 election, is now moving sharply toward Democrats. A recent NBC News/Telemundo poll of 800 registered Latino voters, conducted September 21-28 with a margin of error of 3.5 percentage points, shows that 53% of Latino men prefer Democratic control of Congress, compared to 39% for Republicans. Among all Latino voters, the Democratic edge is 59% to 35%, a 24-point advantage. Trump's approval rating among Latino voters overall stands at 27%, and 33% among Latino men. The poll also reveals that a majority of Latino voters view their congressional vote as a signal against Trump, with nearly two-thirds stating their income is falling behind the cost of living, and 78% disapproving of Trump's handling of economic issues. item.title: Palm Beach County GOP defends campaign for Clerk of Courts charged with child molestation
item.description: The Palm Beach County Republican Party has refused to distance itself from Mike Caruso, a suspended Clerk of Courts who faces criminal charges including lewd or lascivious molestation, kidnapping, child abuse, and luring or enticing a child. Caruso, a former Republican state legislator and longtime ally of Governor Ron DeSantis, was arrested on August 18 by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. Governor DeSantis suspended him immediately following the arrest. The state Republican Party has stated it would not support Caruso's reelection if he remained in the race, but the local GOP committee, led by Chairman Carl Cascio, maintains that it has a 'duty' under state law and local party rules to campaign for party nominees. Cascio stated in a letter posted on the county party's website that the state party directed him to select a replacement candidate after the arrest, and that he remained in close contact with Governor DeSantis's office. item.title: Saudi-led coalition rejects Houthi's false claim of Riyadh attack amid intensified Yemen conflict
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition has dismissed the Houthi armed group's claim of conducting missile and drone attacks on an Aramco oil facility near Riyadh, calling it 'misleading' and an attempt to divert attention from their military losses. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki stated that the Houthis are trying to shift focus from the significant casualties they have suffered and growing public discontent against them. The Yemeni government forces, supported by the Saudi-led coalition, reported executing 257 precision targeting operations against Houthi positions, resulting in an estimated 700 Houthi combatant deaths. The coalition also announced 97 additional precision strikes on Houthi reinforcements in the Tor al-Baha front and Taiz axis. The conflict in Yemen has escalated since the collapse of a fragile 2022 truce in July, leading to the displacement of hundreds of thousands of people. item.title: Fox News Legal Contributor Criticizes Cornell Rape Accuser Over 'Debaucherous Behavior' Claims
item.description: A Fox News legal contributor, Donna Rotunno, who previously defended Harvey Weinstein in his 2020 rape trial, has criticized a woman accusing seven Cornell University fraternity members of gang rape. Rotunno made these remarks on 'Fox & Friends' following a discussion about the case, which involves Jane Doe, a plaintiff in a civil lawsuit alleging that seven former Chi Phi fraternity members drugged and sexually assaulted her in October 2024. No criminal charges have been filed against the accused. Rotunno argued that the accuser should take responsibility for her choices, stating that 'young kids on a college campus making decisions. Decisions to drink, decisions to engage in debaucherous behavior, and there are consequences to that.' She further contended that the accuser's anonymity should not shield her from scrutiny, especially given that her statements in a 2024 sworn statement to Cornell police differed from those in her 2026 lawsuit. item.title: Justice Department Reveals Details of Secret Epstein Training Videos Amid Trump 'Cover-Up' Allegations
item.description: The Justice Department (DOJ) has been compelled to disclose new information regarding secret training videos related to the handling of Jeffrey Epstein's case, which has become central to allegations of a 'cover-up' involving President Donald Trump. According to legal commentator Allison Gill, the DOJ admitted to possessing 75 minutes of training videos designed to instruct FBI officials on how to flag documents containing Trump's name. These videos were initially withheld by the DOJ, which sought to delay their release until after the midterm elections. The DOJ requested a 90-day extension to file a motion to dismiss Gill's lawsuit, but Senior Judge Beryl A. Howell denied the request and ordered the agency to provide more detailed information by September 25. The DOJ's latest filing revealed that the training videos included nine videos, two of which specifically instructed agents to flag documents containing certain high-profile names, including Trump's. item.title: Andy Burnham Affirms RAF Fairford Security Amid U.S. Military Withdrawal Following Terror Plot Concerns
item.description: Andy Burnham, the Mayor of Greater Manchester, has reaffirmed the safety of RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire following the withdrawal of U.S. strategic bombers from the airbase due to security concerns related to a suspected terror plot. The Pentagon announced on October 4, 2026, that all U.S. aircraft stationed at RAF Fairford had been redeployed to their home stations across the Atlantic. This decision came after six individuals were arrested in connection with an alleged plot targeting the military facility. According to The New York Times, U.S. officials cited more specific threat intelligence regarding the base as the reason for the redeployment, which involved aircraft previously engaged in strikes against Iran. The Prime Minister's official spokesman confirmed that RAF Fairford remains secure, stating 'Yes' when asked about the base's safety. item.title: Trump's Doxxing of Senator Cotton Sparks Criticism Ahead of Midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump has sparked criticism for publicly sharing the personal cell phone number of Arkansas Senator Tom Cotton on social media, a move described as a 'pointless fight' just before the midterm elections. The incident occurred as Cotton blocked efforts to fast-track the Sunshine Protection Act, which aims to make daylight saving time permanent and eliminate the twice-yearly clock changes. Trump posted Cotton's number on Truth Social, arguing that Cotton was holding up the bill that 'people want.' However, Cotton has maintained that previous attempts to fix daylight saving time failed and were quickly reversed. Louisiana Senator John Kennedy criticized Trump, stating that the president 'can go from zero to a-hole in about three seconds' and that sharing the senator's number was unhelpful. item.title: Kristi Noem defends immigration policies after '60 Minutes' criticism
item.description: U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, now serving as Donald Trump's special envoy to the Shield of the Americas initiative, reacted angrily to criticism from Republican Senator Thom Tillis on CBS's '60 Minutes' program. During the interview, Tillis criticized Noem's tenure, mentioning the $200 million spent on an ad campaign featuring her riding a horse and questioning her claims about individuals shot being domestic terrorists. Tillis also stated that Noem and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth were 'poster children for men and women who should never have the authority they've been granted.' Noem responded on social media platform X, defending her policies and claiming she saved taxpayers $40 billion by encouraging voluntary departures of undocumented immigrants instead of costly detentions and deportations. item.title: Georgia Election Board Chair Admits Executive Director Overstepped Authority in Federal Election Intervention Request
item.description: The chair of Georgia's State Election Board, John Fervier, admitted to Votebeat that he has no control over his executive director, James Mills, whose letters requesting federal intervention in Georgia's upcoming midterms have caused significant controversy. Mills, the executive director, sent letters to Attorney General Todd Blanche, Civil Rights Division head Harmeet Dhillon, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, asking the Justice Department to impose new security measures before the midterms and to give Georgia a six-month deadline to stop using QR codes for ballot counting. He also urged federal officials to mandate a statewide software update before November, which state election officials claim cannot be completed in time. The board had voted 3-2 on September 28 to authorize Mills to seek federal assistance, over Fervier's objection, granting him broad authority to take actions deemed 'necessary' or 'desirable.' item.title: GIGABYTE Launches 64GB Unified Memory Version of AI TOP ATOM for Desktop AI Development
item.description: GIGABYTE has announced the launch of a new 64GB unified memory version of the AI TOP ATOM, expanding its existing 128GB offering. The new configuration, available starting October 23, 2026, retains the hardware design based on the NVIDIA DGX Spark platform, providing developers, researchers, and enterprise teams with greater flexibility to select configurations that best fit their AI workloads and memory requirements. This desktop AI solution enables users to perform model inference, prototype development, and data analysis in office, laboratory, and educational settings, maintaining control over development resources and project data while reducing reliance on cloud computing. The 64GB version, alongside the existing 128GB model, creates a more comprehensive product lineup, allowing users to evaluate and select memory capacity based on model sizes, workflows, and multitasking needs. item.title: Psychiatrist Warns of Trump's Mental Health Concerns Amid Late-Night Behavior
item.description: A psychiatrist who shared in the 1985 Nobel Peace Prize, Dr. Henry David Abraham, has publicly stated that President Donald Trump exhibits symptoms of mental decline, describing him as 'a maniac at night' and 'a demented grandfather.' In an interview with AlterNet published on Sunday, Abraham, a professor of psychiatry emeritus at Tufts University School of Medicine, highlighted Trump's late-night tweeting sprees as indicative of manic behavior, contrasting it with his apparent drowsiness during the day. Abraham emphasized that frequent late-night activity, such as tweeting 50 to 150 times, is not consistent with normal mental health. He cited a statement from 36 psychiatrists and neurologists, which was entered into the Congressional Record on April 30, warning of Trump's 'rapidly worsening, reality-untethered, increasingly dangerous decline.' item.title: Colorado Republican Faces Backlash Over Epstein File Vote in Tight Re-election Race
item.description: Rep. Jeff Crank (R-CO) is facing increased scrutiny and a new attack ad in his upcoming re-election campaign due to his initial opposition to releasing files related to Jeffrey Epstein. According to The New York Times, Crank actively worked against efforts to make Epstein-related documents public early on, despite ultimately voting to release the files after receiving White House approval. The attack ad, reviewed by the Times, features Sky Roberts, brother of Epstein victim Virginia Giuffre, who died by suicide last year. Roberts accuses Crank of refusing to meet with Giuffre's family and blocking the release of Epstein-related files, stating, 'He has no business being in Congress.' The ad highlights Crank's failure to support a discharge petition led by Reps. Thomas Massie (R-KY) and Ro Khanna (D-CA), which aimed to force the Justice Department to release all Epstein-related files. item.title: Trump's Yemen Bombing Campaign and Hasty Truce Led to Houthi Resurgence, Analysts Say
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration initiated a military campaign against Yemen's Houthi militants in March 2025, known as Operation Rough Rider, which lasted 51 days and cost over $1 billion. The operation targeted more than 1,000 sites, but the Houthis continued to attack U.S. warships and shot down seven MQ-9 Reaper drones, while the U.S. lost two F/A-18 fighter jets in accidents. The campaign was marred by the 'Signalgate' scandal, where Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth shared classified details of the strikes in a Signal group chat that accidentally included journalist Jeffrey Goldberg, creating a risk to operational security. The administration began seeking an exit just weeks into the operation, taking a truce offered by Oman without a clear strategy. Trump declared victory in May 2025, claiming the Houthis 'don't want to fight anymore,' but the administration neglected Yemen afterward, failing to fill a special envoy position and slashing aid. item.title: Brazilian Federal Police Investigate U.S. Election Interference in Presidential Race
item.description: Brazil's Federal Police have launched an investigation into alleged U.S. interference in Brazil's presidential election, following reports that the Trump administration planned to divert taxpayer funds to support groups opposing Brazil's judicial system. The investigation, announced Sunday, involves the seizure of computer equipment and communications in São Paulo, Brazil's largest city, as part of a probe into 'possible external interference by the United States' in the nation's election. The first-round presidential election held on Sunday saw Flávio Bolsonaro, a far-right politician backed by Donald Trump, secure 47% of the vote compared to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 45.1%, forcing a runoff between the two candidates. Bolsonaro, son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro who is currently serving a 27-year sentence for an attempted coup, has been a vocal supporter of Trump, who has criticized Brazil's judicial system and called for the release of his ally.

item.title: Trump Envoy Accused of Sexual Assault in Lawsuit Involving Melania Trump Connection
item.description: A longtime friend of Donald Trump, Paolo Zampolli, who has claimed to have introduced the president to Melania Trump, is facing a civil lawsuit alleging he drugged and sexually assaulted a woman at his Manhattan townhouse. The lawsuit, filed by tech entrepreneur Victoria Drake, 33, claims that on October 5, 2023, Zampolli approached her at the Zero Bond private members' club in Manhattan, where he recognized her from Mar-a-Lago events. After exchanging numbers, they met at Zampolli's Gramercy Park home, where Drake alleges he gave her a drink that caused her to lose consciousness. She claims she woke up naked in bed with Zampolli sexually assaulting her while holding her neck, stating she did not and could not consent. Drake reported the incident to the NYPD the following day and was taken to Lenox Health Greenwich Hospital for exams. item.title: Trump Administration Ends 75-Year U.S.-UK Military Partnership Following Security Concerns at RAF Fairford
item.description: The Trump administration has reportedly ended a 75-year military partnership between the United States and the United Kingdom following security concerns at RAF Fairford, a British air base used by the U.S. for decades. According to NBC News, the U.S. has withdrawn all bomber aircraft, including B-1, B-2, and B-52 models, from the base and redeployed them to U.S. home stations. The decision came after local authorities declared a 'major incident' at RAF Fairford, leading to the evacuation of nearby residents and the arrest of five men suspected of involvement in a potential terror plot under the Explosives Act. The withdrawal, described as 'rushed' and 'hasty' by media outlets, has left many journalists and analysts stunned. item.title: Trump's Pardon Promise for Officials Near Oval Office Sparks Political Tensions
item.description: President Donald Trump has pledged to preemptively pardon anyone who has come 'within 200 feet' of the Oval Office before he leaves office, a promise that could lead to a clash with Democrats who are considering prosecuting administration officials for misusing their authority. The Washington Post reported that Democrats are drafting legislation to rein in the powers Trump has expanded, particularly focusing on Justice Department actions targeting Trump's political enemies, which some argue may be illegal and expose officials to criminal charges. Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD) emphasized the need for a 'massive reconstruction task' to undo Trump's changes, which he believes will take decades. Raskin has drafted bills to bar presidents from accepting foreign government payments without congressional consent, require public review of White House renovations, and prevent presidents from reaching monetary settlements with their own government. item.title: Trump Confuses Brazil with India in Late-Night Criticism of U.S. Election Integrity
item.description: President Donald Trump made a notable error during a late-night social media post, mistakenly referring to Brazil's presidential election as India's. The post, which was published at 6:18 AM ET on October 5, 2026, criticized the U.S. election process, claiming that voting results in America take weeks to calculate while Brazil's results were available the same day. Trump wrote, '125 Million People voted today in the first round of Brazil's Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the SAME DAY!' He then contrasted this with U.S. cities like Detroit, Philadelphia, and California, where results with smaller numbers often take weeks to 'Rig, I mean, calculate.' The post was later corrected from 'India' to 'Brazil' after Newsweek reported that the original version contained the error. item.title: Texas Stock Exchange aims to challenge Wall Street dominance as financial firms expand in Dallas
item.description: The Texas Stock Exchange is positioning itself as a new competitor to Wall Street and Nasdaq, aiming to establish Texas as America's next financial hub. The Dallas-based exchange has already secured primary listings from major companies including Energy Transfer, Dillard's, Sunoco, and Texas Capital Bank. Former Representative Jeb Hensarling, a strategic advisor to the Texas Stock Exchange, argues that Texas has become the 'economic center of gravity' in America, attracting businesses due to its pro-business policies, lower taxes, and lighter regulation compared to traditional financial centers like New York. item.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is conducting a clinical trial of Gilead Sciences' experimental drug obeldesivir to evaluate its effectiveness in preventing Ebola virus disease following exposure to the Bundibugyo virus. The trial, known as EBO-PEP, is being carried out in Ituri province, where an Ebola outbreak emerged in mid-May 2026. More than 250 individuals are currently participating in the study, with plans to enroll approximately 1,000 adults and children aged 12 and older. Participants must have had contact with someone who tested positive for the Bundibugyo virus within the past five days and must not yet show symptoms. The study is coordinated by the medical humanitarian organization ALIMA, in collaboration with the DRC's National Institute for Biomedical Research and the French organization ANRS. item.title: George Armfield: Victorian Era Dog Painter Celebrated for Detailed Animal Art
item.description: George Armfield (c. 1808–1893) was a British animal painter renowned for his vivid and meticulously detailed portrayals of dogs during the Victorian era. Born George Armfield Smith, he was the son of portrait painter William Armfield Hobday and began exhibiting his work at the Royal Academy at a young age. Specializing in genre scenes featuring terriers, hounds, and other domestic dogs, Armfield captured the energy, character, and everyday behaviors of these animals through broad, expressive brushstrokes. His paintings, which depicted dogs hunting, playing, or resting in rural settings such as barns and fields, were immensely popular with Victorian audiences and remain among the most celebrated examples of 19th-century British animal art. The article highlights several of Armfield's notable works, including 'Dog with Puppies,' 'Gun Dogs in the Long Grass,' 'Spaniel Flushing Pheasant,' 'Three Spaniels and a Flying Mallard,' and 'Two Dogs Resting by Their Master's Lunch Basket.' item.title: US withdraws bombers from RAF Fairford amid security concerns over suspected terror plot
item.description:
The United States Air Force has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, a military air base in Gloucestershire, England, following a suspected terror plot targeting the facility. A Pentagon official confirmed on Sunday that the bombers, which included B-1, B-2, and B-52 aircraft, have been redeployed to their home stations in the United States. The decision comes after British authorities arrested multiple individuals in connection with an alleged terrorist attack planned for the base.
On September 27, five UK nationals in their mid-20s were arrested on suspicion of explosives offenses and terrorism near the military site. They have since been released on bail, along with a sixth suspect, a dual British-Iranian national, who was arrested on October 1 on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. CEO Andrew Boyd revealed in an exclusive WIRED interview that Paragon cannot see who customers target or the data they extract from devices, relying instead on customer vetting and contractual agreements to prevent abuse. item.description: The WIRED publication has launched an interactive feature that simulates the experience of traveling in the Occupied West Bank. This digital tool provides users with a virtual journey through the region, highlighting the challenges and restrictions faced by travelers in this politically sensitive area. The interactive map and multimedia content aim to educate the public about the complex realities of life under occupation, including checkpoints, restricted movement, and the impact on daily routines. item.title: Glynis Johns' Mermaid Role in 'Miranda' (1948) Featured Unique Rubber Tail Design and Practical Effects
item.description: The article discusses a collection of 20 photographs showcasing Glynis Johns as a mermaid in the 1948 British fantasy comedy film 'Miranda.' Johns portrayed the character Miranda Trewella, a playful and flirtatious mermaid, through specialized practical effects, unique wardrobe designs, and her personal charm. A notable aspect of her transformation was the construction of her mermaid tail, which was designed by The Dunlop Rubber Company. Dunlop created two separate rubber tails for the production: one for swimming scenes that prioritized movement and buoyancy, and another for dry scenes that was designed to be worn with custom gowns. The rubber tail was extremely heavy, immobilizing Johns' legs, requiring crew members and co-stars to physically carry her around the studio lot. item.description: The U.S. military conducted a lethal strike on a vessel in the Caribbean that was suspected of carrying drug traffickers, resulting in the deaths of four individuals on board. The military shared a video showing what appeared to be an explosion destroying the moving vessel. This change aims to encourage large-scale data center development in rural communities, though experts warn that the benefits may not necessarily translate into job creation or local economic growth. The opportunity zone program, initially proposed during the Trump administration, has faced criticism for not effectively driving investment to disadvantaged areas. item.description: Animal welfare organizations are raising concerns about the Utah Department of Agriculture and Food's handling of a bird flu outbreak at a mink farm in Salt Lake County. The outbreak, which has been confirmed in seven captive mink cases as of August, marks the first documented instance of avian influenza in mink in the United States. Advocacy groups, including Animal Wellness Action and the Center for a Humane Economy, have criticized the state's lack of transparency, demanding detailed information on mink-to-mink transmission, worker exposure, and the farm's population. item.title: Security Flaw in ChatGPT's macOS App Allows Potential Data Theft by Attackers
item.description: A recently discovered vulnerability in the macOS version of OpenAI's ChatGPT application has been patched, but it could have allowed attackers to gain access to sensitive user data. The flaw, identified by researchers at the Objective-See Foundation, exploited a trusted component within the app that could be manipulated to deliver untrusted scripts into the main ChatGPT process. This would have enabled attackers to access chat logs, browser sessions, and other stored data, as well as potentially run commands through the application. The vulnerability required an attacker to already have malware installed on a target machine, making it a local exploit. Patrick Wardle, a software analyst at Objective-See, described the flaw as 'insanely trivial' to exploit, requiring only about a dozen lines of code for a proof of concept. item.description:
The Prime Minister of Samoa, Laaulialemalietoa Lea Schmidt, has issued a public apology after a video surfaced showing him performing a Nazi salute and leading a chant of 'Heil Hitler' at a private family gathering in 2007. In the brief seven-second clip, Schmidt can be seen instructing approximately a dozen attendees to raise their right hands in the salute while saying 'Heil Hitler,' with the group complying.
The video was first reported by the Samoa Observer on Sunday, prompting Schmidt to release an official government statement on Monday expressing regret. He acknowledged that regardless of his intentions at the time, the words and actions were inappropriate and could cause offense and pain. Schmidt emphasized that the comments were never meant for public view and stated that the incident does not reflect his personal beliefs or those of the Samoan government.

item.description: The article discusses the growing prominence of Black Twitter on the social media platform Threads, highlighting how it has become a vital hub for Black social media users following the decline of Twitter (now X) under Elon Musk's ownership. Chris Rhodes, 47, the owner of the property, denied being a 'neighbour from hell' despite the severe consequences for his neighbor, Shivarna Mitra, 44. Mitra, who moved into the property in 2021 after recovering from cancer, had invested £80,000 in renovations, intending to make it her 'forever home' with her mother and young son. However, Rhodes began demolishing his half of the house in 2022 without proper planning permission, claiming he was following health and safety guidelines after a storm made the gable wall unsafe. The company announced on October 1 that the program would be paused until the first quarter of 2027, citing a 'significant rise' in automated submissions that were largely invalid or contained hallucinations. item.title: Primordial Magnetic Fields May Resolve Hubble Tension in Cosmic Expansion Measurements
item.description:
Scientists have discovered that tiny magnetic fields generated shortly after the Big Bang could help explain the long-standing discrepancy in measurements of the universe's expansion rate. This 'Hubble tension' arises from two different methods of measuring the Hubble constant, which describes how fast the universe is expanding. One method, based on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observed by telescopes like Planck, predicts a Hubble constant of approximately 67 kilometers per second per megaparsec (km/s/Mpc). The other method, which measures the brightness of Type Ia supernovae in distant galaxies, yields a higher value of about 73 km/s/Mpc. The difference between these measurements is statistically significant and suggests that our current cosmological model may be incomplete.

He argues that the Supreme Court would likely defer to the political process rather than intervene in a constitutional dispute over Trump's eligibility. Mehlhorn suggests that even if the Court were to rule Trump ineligible, the 'political question' doctrine would prevent them from enforcing such a decision, potentially allowing Trump to assume the presidency through a de facto outcome. The article notes that Trump has repeatedly suggested seeking a third term despite constitutional limitations, and some allies like Steve Bannon have claimed he could circumvent these restrictions. item.title: Oasis take legal action to halt auction of rare unreleased recordings
item.description: Oasis has taken legal action to stop the planned auction of a large archive of previously unheard recordings associated with the band. The collection, known as The Desk Tapes, was assembled by Huw Richards, Oasis’s former front-of-house sound engineer, who worked with the group from 1994 until 2001. It was scheduled to be sold by Littleton Auctions on October 3, with a guide price of £1.2 million to £1.6 million. The archive reportedly included 63 concert recordings, more than 100 hours of rehearsal material, soundchecks, and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher. Following legal proceedings brought by Oasis, the Gallaghers, and Sony Music Entertainment U.K., the auction house withdrew the lot from the sale. Littleton Auctions’ managing director, Ben Homer, said the recordings had been removed in light of the legal action and expressed disappointment that the archive could not be offered as planned. item.description: Ex-Doctor Who showrunner Russell T. Davies has publicly addressed the detrimental impact of online leaks on the franchise, stating that they have 'more ferocious than ever' and are 'hurting the run' of the show. This widespread leaking has led to fan cynicism, with audiences becoming less surprised by storylines and quicker to assume new ideas would fail. Davies specifically links the decision to cancel the 2026 Christmas Special to the leaks, as the BBC feared public backlash and potential legal action. The BBC was reportedly hesitant to pursue legal action against the leaker, fearing it would appear disproportionate to prosecute a member of the public for copyright infringement. item.description: Brazil's presidential election has set up a rematch between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who finished first and second in the opening round. item.description: The 1956 Auto Union DKW F93, also known as the 'Big DKW 3=6,' was a notable West German automobile manufactured by Auto Union. This vehicle was powered by a three-cylinder two-stroke engine producing 38 horsepower, which was marketed with the slogan '3=6,' suggesting performance equivalent to a six-cylinder four-stroke engine. The F93 featured a wider body compared to its predecessor, an oval front grille, enhanced suspension, and front-wheel drive. It was available in multiple body styles, including sedan, coupe, and a limited cabriolet version, blending practical design with the unique characteristics of two-stroke engineering. Produced until 1959, the DKW F93 stands as a significant example of postwar German automotive innovation. The car's distinctive style and engineering are captured in the photographs provided, highlighting its role as a unique classic of the 1950s. item.description: A recent incident involving a Trump voter from Ohio, Jack Buhring, who struck and killed a 20-year-old Haitian immigrant named Pierre Damas Bel, has brought attention to the harsh realities of the Trump administration's immigration policies. item.title: Developers submit £16.5 billion data centre plan for former Chapelcross nuclear site in Scotland
item.description:
Developers have submitted planning proposals for a £16.5 billion data centre campus at the former Chapelcross nuclear power station near Annan in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. CX Tech Limited is seeking permission to build what it describes as a 'net-zero technology campus' comprising eight data centres with a combined capacity of approximately 1 gigawatt, which would make it one of the largest data centre facilities in the world by power capacity.
The project is expected to create around 750 construction jobs and more than 500 permanent full-time positions once operational. Construction is proposed to begin in 2027, with completion targeted within eight years. The developer states the campus will cover 162,000 square metres and will be powered entirely by locally and regionally generated renewable energy, including wind, solar and biomass sources connected via direct and private-wire arrangements.

item.title: Looney Tunes Film 'Coyote vs. Acme' Surpasses $100 Million at Box Office, Challenges Warner Bros. Decision
item.description: The Looney Tunes comedy 'Coyote vs. Acme,' which was shelved by Warner Bros. as a tax write-off and later rescued by indie distributor Ketchup Entertainment, has grossed over $100 million globally. The film, starring Will Forte and John Cena and produced by DC Studios co-chief James Gunn, was initially deemed financially unworthy by Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav, who decided against a theatrical release. Despite a $70 million production cost, the film has earned $59.8 million domestically and $45 million internationally, outperforming other Ketchup-distributed Looney Tunes films like 'The Day the Earth Blew Up,' which grossed only $15.4 million globally. Analysts suggest that Warner Bros. may have missed an opportunity by not investing in stronger marketing, as the film's success was partly driven by positive word of mouth and strong reviews. item.title: Sen. John Kennedy Criticizes Trump for Publicly Sharing Senator Tom Cotton's Cell Number
item.description: Senator John Kennedy (R-La.) has publicly criticized President Donald Trump for sharing the cell phone number of fellow Republican Senator Tom Cotton (R-Ark.) on Truth Social. The incident occurred after Cotton blocked a bill to make daylight saving time permanent, known as the Sunshine Protection Act. Trump posted Cotton's number on his Truth Social account, urging supporters to call him to 'let him know' about the House-passed bill. Kennedy, speaking on NBC's 'Meet the Press,' referred to Trump as his 'friend' but expressed disapproval of the president's decision to publicly disclose Cotton's personal contact information. Kennedy stated, 'I don't think he should have given out Tom's cell phone number. I don't think that's going to help convince Tom,' adding that Trump 'exists loudly' and can be 'tempestuous,' noting he 'can go from zero to a-hole in about three seconds.' item.title: US Marine Arrested in Okinawa for Alleged Murder and Burglary of 39-Year-Old Woman
item.description: A U.S. Marine was arrested in Okinawa, Japan, on suspicion of burglary and murder, sparking widespread outrage both in Japan and internationally. According to The Associated Press, the 29-year-old service member was taken into custody for allegedly killing a 39-year-old woman in a hotel in Naha, the capital of Okinawa, and stealing her wallet and belongings afterward. Police footage reportedly showed the Marine entering the hotel with the victim and leaving alone. The incident has caused significant tension between the U.S. and Japan, with Okinawa Governor Genta Koja stating that the case "deals a major shock and adds fear to the Okinawans who have already been forced to live next to U.S. bases." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi condemned the incident in a statement to CNN, calling it "an extremely brutal and heinous incident" and expressing "profound regret," while also noting that the Japanese government has lodged a strong protest with the U.S. side. item.description: Aaron Sorkin, the acclaimed screenwriter and director, has shared his thoughts on Jesse Eisenberg's decision to decline the role of Mark Zuckerberg in his upcoming film 'The Social Reckoning,' which serves as a follow-up to his 2010 film 'The Social Network.' However, Eisenberg ultimately declined, stating he was moving in different directions in his life and didn't want to be associated with the character. item.description: The Baltimore Ravens secured a 24-7 halftime lead over the Tennessee Titans before halftime, with quarterback Lamar Jackson suffering an ankle injury in the first half. Despite initial concerns, Jackson was not ruled out for the remainder of the game and was seen smiling on the sideline, indicating the injury was not as severe as feared. Head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson was dealing with 'a little bit of an ankle' and that the team was not overly concerned. The Ravens chose to hold back Jackson for the second half, relying on backup quarterback Tyler Huntley to close out the game. This decision was based on the Ravens' confidence in their lead and the Titans' poor performance, as the Titans entered the game with a 0-4 record and the third-worst scoring average in the NFL at 12.3 points per game. item.title: Attorney Says Cornell Student Alleging Sexual Assault Has Received Threats
item.description:
A former Cornell University student who alleges that she was sexually assaulted by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity is facing threats intended to pressure her to withdraw a civil lawsuit, according to her attorney, Thomas Giuffra. The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, alleges that the assault occurred overnight on October 19–20, 2024, while she was under the influence of ketamine, alcohol, and marijuana.
Giuffra said that individuals attempting to identify Jane Doe have also targeted at least three women who were mistakenly identified as the accuser. He said both his client and other women have received threats, and he reported that he himself had been threatened. Giuffra did not identify those responsible or say whether the threats had been reported to law enforcement.

item.description: A truck driver who voted for Donald Trump for the first time in 2024 is grappling with guilt after his vehicle struck and killed a 20-year-old Haitian immigrant named Pierre Damas Bel near Springfield, Ohio, on August 31, 2026. Bel, who had Temporary Protected Status (TPS) due to instability in Haiti, lost his legal status when the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to end TPS for Haitians. Buhring described the moment of impact, stating he felt a 'big thump' and could feel the collision. He also mentioned making eye contact with Bel before the accident. item.description: Brazilians participated in a pivotal presidential election on Sunday, October 4, 2026, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva facing off against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. item.title: Vietnamese NASA Scientist Advances Miniaturization of Atomic Clocks for Deep Space Missions
item.description: Vietnamese-born scientist Hoang Thai, a principal investigator at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in California, is leading research to develop ultra-precise atomic clocks that can withstand the extreme conditions of deep space. The team's work focuses on miniaturizing quantum sensors, which use atomic properties and quantum phenomena to measure time, gravity, electromagnetic fields, and other physical variables with exceptional accuracy. Current quantum setups are typically confined to laboratories due to their reliance on delicate lasers, vacuum chambers, magnetic shielding, and strictly controlled environments. Thai's team aims to overcome the 'SWaP' challenge—optimizing size, weight, and power consumption—to create compact, rugged clocks suitable for spacecraft. One of their projects involves scaling down a microwave clock to the size of a one-liter container, with potential applications for future GPS satellites. item.description: President Donald Trump's administration has come under fire for its handling of government-funded political advertisements, particularly after CNN anchor Jake Tapper flagged a political ad supporting Trump that aired during an NFL game. The game focuses on cleaning and redecorating a castle room by room, requiring players to put items in their rightful places, remove dirt and rubbish, and repair banners and rugs. item.description: The final online post of Simon Andriesz, a British banker who exposed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's business connections to Jeffrey Epstein, has resurfaced, sparking renewed concern over his recent death. item.description: The article discusses the rarity of rockets achieving more than 20 launches per year, with SpaceX's Falcon 9 being the only rocket to exceed 50 launches from a single launch pad. It highlights that only China and SpaceX currently have over 50 launches annually, with China employing a Russian-style approach using multiple launch pads and expendable rockets. The piece details SpaceX's journey to achieving high launch reliability, noting that the Falcon 9 reached approximately 90% reliability through 2016, following incidents like the CRS-7 loss in 2015 and the AMOS-6 pad loss in 2016. After returning to flight in January 2017, the Falcon 9 operated without failure until Block 5 entered service in May 2018. By 2019-2020, the cumulative success rate had reached 95%, with the statistical lower bound approaching 98%. item.title: Oil Prices and Inflation Expectations Drive Global Bond-Market Turmoil as Debt Risks Persist
item.description:
Global bond markets are facing renewed turmoil as investors reassess the outlook for inflation, interest rates, and government borrowing. Soaring oil prices have emerged as a clear catalyst for the recent rise in bond yields, because more expensive energy can push consumer prices higher and make it more difficult for central banks to reduce interest rates. Higher expected inflation generally lowers the appeal of existing bonds, whose fixed payments become less valuable in real terms, leading investors to demand higher yields.
Government debt levels are also drawing increased attention. Many countries have accumulated substantial debt, limiting their fiscal flexibility and raising concerns about how governments will finance future deficits. If investors become less confident in a government’s ability to manage its debt burden, they may demand additional compensation for holding that country’s bonds. item.description:
Kerala's Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has ordered a Vigilance investigation into allegations of irregularities during the tenure of current Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as the state's Public Works Department (PWD) Secretary. item.title: Meta Claims Billions in Tax Credits by Classifying AI Data Centers as Experimental
item.description:
Meta is using an aggressive tax strategy to claim billions of dollars in research and experimentation tax credits by classifying its AI data centers as experimental pilot models, according to people familiar with the company's operations. The approach allows Meta to receive taxpayer subsidies for expensive computer chips from companies like Nvidia, even though these components are commercially proven technology widely used across the industry.
The tax break, created during the Reagan administration in the 1980s, was designed to encourage American companies to take risks on uncertain technological innovations. Companies must meet a complex four-part test proving they are conducting genuine experiments rather than standard business operations. While thousands of companies benefit from this credit, they typically claim it for researcher and engineer salaries, not for physical infrastructure and equipment.

By age five, he was already performing with his parents, Joe and Myra Keaton, in a physically demanding act where his father would throw him around the stage, drop him down stairs, and hurl him into the audience or through windows. To ensure safety, Buster had a hidden suitcase handle sewn into his costumes for precise handling. The company plans to launch its SR75 suborbital vehicle in spring 2027, depending on the completion of remaining operational requirements and favorable weather conditions. The SR75 is a lightweight, aerodynamically stabilized suborbital rocket intended for research and technology demonstration missions, including applications related to microgravity and hypersonic flight. It is not designed to deploy satellites. The license followed a regulatory review of HyImpulse’s systems and safety procedures. item.description: The article discusses how Donald Trump's military actions and policies have inadvertently accelerated the global transition to renewable energy sources. The author, Thom Hartmann, argues that Trump's decision to engage in a conflict that has driven up oil prices has led to a significant reduction in global oil demand, with the International Energy Agency reporting a 2.5% annual decrease in oil consumption, equivalent to removing 42 million gas-powered vehicles from roads. item.title: Oregon Man Trapped by Boulder Uses Earbuds to Call for Rescue
item.description:
Joseph Little, a 28-year-old Oregon resident, was rescued after a large boulder pinned him against rocks near the Marina in Warrenton, Oregon. The incident occurred early on September 26 while Little was on an uneven section of jetty extending into the Columbia River, approximately 90 miles northwest of Portland.
According to Sgt. Dylan McCoy of the Warrenton Police Department, the boulder became dislodged and fell onto Little, trapping his upper body and legs. Although authorities did not know the rock’s exact weight, McCoy estimated that it weighed about a ton. The boulder landed near an area where high tide regularly pushes water over the rocks, creating a serious risk that Little could drown if help did not arrive quickly.

item.title: Brazilian Bellbirds and Seriemas Among the Loudest Birds Ever Recorded
item.description:
A new scientific study has identified some of the loudest birds ever documented, with vocalizations that surpass the noise of jackhammers, chainsaws, and even elephant trumpets. The research, led by evolutionary biologist João Mes and published in the journal Evolution, focused on two Brazilian species: the bare-throated bellbird and the red-legged seriema.
Despite being only about the size of a dove, the bare-throated bellbird produces sharp, metallic calls from the canopy of Brazil's Serra do Mar mountains that can overwhelm listeners. These calls, used primarily to attract mates, rank among the most deafening sounds ever recorded in the avian world. The red-legged seriema matches this volume, joining a previously recognized bellbird species as one of the loudest birds known to science.
The researchers also discovered several anatomical features that enable these birds to produce such powerful songs, offering new insights into the mechanics of avian vocalizations. The findings chal

item.title: Alert, the World's Northernmost Inhabited Place
item.description: Alert, located on Ellesmere Island in Nunavut, Canada, is recognized as the northernmost permanently inhabited settlement on Earth. Situated at approximately 82°30'N latitude, this remote outpost serves as a critical research station for environmental and climate studies. The community, established in 1950 as a military base, now supports a small population of scientists and support staff who conduct year-round research on Arctic ecosystems, atmospheric conditions, and climate change. Despite its extreme location, Alert has basic amenities including a small store, a post office, and a medical facility. The area experiences six months of continuous daylight in summer and six months of darkness in winter, creating unique challenges for residents. The settlement's isolation and harsh climate make it a vital location for understanding the impacts of global warming on polar regions. item.title: Trump Administration Forms UFO Advisory Panel to Review Unidentified Aerial Phenomena
item.description: The New York Times reports that President Donald Trump’s administration has created a new advisory council focused on unidentified anomalous phenomena, commonly known as UAPs or UFOs. The panel, formed during the administration’s release of government records on the subject, includes scientists who are open to the possibility that some sightings could involve extraterrestrial technology. Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb chairs the group and has argued that even a single confirmed case of alien technological origin would represent an extraordinary scientific discovery. The administration has released files that include previously surfaced military footage, reports, and government material discussing topics such as interstellar wormholes. Trump said the records were being made public so people could assess the information themselves. item.title: Brewers Secure NLDS Game 1 Victory Following Controversial Home Run Call at American Family Field
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the San Diego Padres 3-2 in Game 1 of the National League Division Series (NLDS) at American Family Field, securing a crucial victory in the best-of-five playoff series. The game featured a dramatic and controversial moment in the seventh inning when Brewers catcher William Contreras hit a solo home run off Padres pitcher Adrian Morejon, which proved to be the decisive run. Contreras' home run, his second hit against San Diego pitching this season, came after a tense sequence where the Brewers had loaded the bases with two outs. The game remained tied until Contreras' hit, which gave Milwaukee a 3-2 lead. The Padres had a chance to tie the game in the ninth inning when first baseman Ty France appeared to hit a go-ahead two-run home run, but the ball struck a truss in the stadium's roof and bounced down, where it was caught by Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio. item.title: Republicans Struggle to Find an Effective Campaign Target for the 2026 Midterms
item.description: Republicans are struggling to identify a single, consistently effective Democratic target for the 2026 midterm elections, according to a POLITICO review of campaign advertising in competitive House and Senate races. In past cycles, figures such as Joe Biden and Nancy Pelosi served as powerful symbols that Republican candidates could use to energize conservative voters and frame Democrats as out of touch. This year, however, those familiar targets have lost some of their political usefulness. Biden remains the Democrat most frequently mentioned in Republican advertisements, appearing across dozens of races, but his lower public profile since leaving office has made him a less potent foil than he was during the 2024 campaign. At a comparable point in that cycle, Biden had been referenced in more than 1,000 Republican House and Senate ads, according to AdImpact data cited by POLITICO. item.title: Ted Cruz responds to JD Vance's 2028 comments, emphasizes focus on 2026 midterms
item.description:
Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) has publicly responded to Vice President JD Vance's suggestion that Cruz is already campaigning for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination. In a phone interview on Saturday, Cruz called Vance 'insecure' and stated that he is instead concentrating on helping Republicans win the upcoming 2026 midterm elections, which are approximately 30 days away. Cruz remarked that people typically engage in political attacks when they are feeling insecure, and he welcomed Vance to make any comments he wishes while Cruz remains focused on Election Day victories.
The exchange began after Vance, in an NBC News interview on Thursday, asserted that it was 'really obvious' that Cruz was running for president at that very moment. Vance contrasted this with his own position, stating that he is not currently campaigning and is instead working to help elect Republicans. item.title: Kyle Gordon Brings Craft and Catchiness to Modern Musical Parody
item.description: Kyle Gordon, a Brooklyn-based musician and comedian, has emerged as one of the most distinctive musical parodists of his generation. His song “Mr. Jambo,” a playful riff on Paul Simon’s “Graceland,” became a social-media hit by combining a highly infectious melody with detailed references to the original album and a pointed commentary on American cultural tourism. The piece demonstrates Gordon’s central strength: he does not simply mock familiar music, but recreates its sound with enough care that the parody can become memorable in its own right. The New York Times describes Gordon as a millennial counterpart to “Weird Al” Yankovic, while noting that the comparison is incomplete. Unlike broad, silly parody, Gordon’s work is nerdy, precise, and deeply engaged with overlooked corners of pop-music history. His third album, “Kyle Gordon Is Everywhere,” was released on Friday and includes “Mr. Jambo.” The record draws on a wide range of styles, including early-2000s indie sleaze, Disney-inf

item.title: UK Financial Sector Intensifies Opposition to Potential Bank Tax Increases in Budget
item.description: Leading figures in the UK financial sector are preparing a coordinated campaign against possible tax increases on banks in Chancellor John Healey’s upcoming Budget. According to Sky News, executives and trade associations—including AFME, UK Finance, and TheCityUK—are drafting a letter warning that additional bank taxes could fail to generate meaningful extra revenue for the Treasury. Their central argument is that higher taxes may push financial businesses, investment, and jobs out of the United Kingdom, weakening London’s competitiveness as an international financial center. The lobbying effort comes shortly before bank chiefs are scheduled to meet Healey in person, with leaders from major institutions such as Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds Banking Group, and NatWest reportedly invited. Industry groups are concerned that the government could raise the bank corporation tax surcharge or introduce other sector-specific measures to help fund public spending or tax reductions elsewhere. item.title: Meta's Muse AI Assistant Builds Comprehensive Relationship Profiles Using User Data
item.description: Meta's new AI assistant, Muse, has become a viral sensation with millions of downloads, allowing users to connect it to bank accounts, messages, and health data to complete tasks. However, researchers have uncovered that Muse creates detailed profiles of all the people in a user's life, including family, friends, colleagues, and partners. By analyzing Muse's internal files, researchers discovered that the AI system compiles information about relationships, such as where people live, what they do, recurring events like apartment moves or shared savings goals, and important dates like birthdays or anniversaries. Muse's documentation indicates that these profiles start sparse and gradually fill out over time, with sections including Facts, History, The Relationship, In Common, Open Threads, and Strengthening. The AI is designed to make suggestions for improving relationships, such as suggesting a date to remember or a reason to call someone. Meta claims Muse gathers context from public in

item.title: Musicians and A.I. Put Human Songwriting to the Test
item.description: New York Times reporter Matt Richtel, who is also an occasional songwriter, describes an experiment comparing human-made music with songs generated by artificial intelligence. He and four experienced musicians spent a weekend in a recording studio composing and producing several songs largely from scratch. The goal was not simply to determine whether people could create music better than A.I., but to examine what makes the two creative processes different and whether human effort still has meaning when machines can produce songs quickly. The article frames the project as a direct contest between human musicians and digital systems, with readers invited to listen to the resulting pieces and judge them. item.title: Navy Transitions From C-2 Greyhound To CMV-22B For Carrier Resupply Missions
item.description: The US Navy has retired the Grumman C-2A Greyhound, which served as the carrier onboard delivery (COD) aircraft for 60 years, and replaced it with the Bell Aircraft Corporation CMV-22B, a modified version of the V-22 Osprey tiltrotor. The Greyhound, a twin-engine turboprop designed for catapult launches and arrested landings on aircraft carriers, was retired after its final two aircraft performed their last carrier landings and catapult launches aboard the USS Nimitz on June 25. The CMV-22B offers significant advantages over the Greyhound, including a wider cargo bay that can transport F-35C engine modules without disassembly, vertical takeoff and landing capabilities that allow it to service smaller surface combatants and remote outposts directly, and the ability to perform vertical replenishment (VERTREP) operations. item.title: China and Russia conduct joint military exercise integrating drones, robotics, and electronic warfare
item.description: China and Russia have conducted a large-scale multinational military exercise called Centre-2026, involving over 47,000 personnel from multiple Shanghai Cooperation Organisation countries. The exercise, held in Russia's Chelyabinsk region, incorporated lessons from the Ukraine conflict, particularly emphasizing the use of drones, electronic warfare, and unmanned ground systems. Chinese forces, traveling by road, rail, and air, participated in reconnaissance, targeting, obstacle breaching, and medical drills before the main operational phase. The drills featured coordinated attacks using a 'small-group, multi-waves' approach, with drone swarms providing targeting information to ground units. item.title: Yankees Drop ALDS Game 1 to Rays Despite Austin Wells' Double That Ended in a Double Play
item.description: The New York Yankees suffered a 1-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1 of the American League Division Series (ALDS) on October 3, 2026, at Tropicana Field. The decisive moment came in the eighth inning when Austin Wells doubled with two outs, breaking up Drew Rasmussen's no-hit bid. However, Wells attempted to stretch the double into a triple and was thrown out at third base by a relay from Victor Mesa Jr. to Taylor Walls to Junior Caminero, ending the Yankees' best scoring opportunity. Rasmussen pitched eight scoreless innings, allowing only one hit and two walks while striking out 10 batters on 101 pitches. He continued his dominance over the Yankees, having nearly no-hit them in a regular-season game at Yankee Stadium. The Rays' only run came in the third inning when Jonathan Aranda hit a 417-foot home run off Gerrit Cole. item.description: U.S. Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR), Chairman of the Senate (Select) Intelligence Committee, has been inundated with phone calls and payment requests following President Donald Trump's public sharing of what he claimed was Cotton's phone number. The incident occurred amid a political dispute over the Sunshine Protection Act, a bill aiming to make daylight saving time permanent. Trump criticized Cotton for being one of the few GOP senators opposing the bill, arguing that Arkansans do not want their children attending school in the dark. After Trump shared the phone number, a journalist discovered a Venmo account linked to the same number, leading to a surge of payment requests from various individuals and figures. item.title: Nike Shares Fall on Weak Outlook as Tesla Sales Beat Expectations
item.description:
Nike, Tesla, and Volvo Car were among the companies drawing investor attention in the latest market session. Nike shares declined after the athletic apparel company warned that revenue is expected to continue falling during the current fiscal year. The company identified China as a particularly difficult market, despite the country remaining its second-largest market worldwide. The warning reinforced concerns about Nike’s ongoing struggles with weak demand, intense competition, and a difficult recovery in China. Investors are likely to focus on whether the company can stabilize sales, improve its product lineup, and restore momentum in one of its most important international markets.

item.title: Trucking Industry Faces Bankruptcies Amid Rising Diesel Costs Linked to Trump's Foreign Policy
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported that over a dozen small trucking operators have filed for bankruptcy in the past month due to soaring diesel prices, which have risen to $6.36 per gallon, up $2.65 from a year ago. Truck drivers are resorting to extreme cost-saving measures, such as cooking meals in their cabs, sleeping at trailer parking spots to avoid overnight fees, and waiting for rain to clean their trucks instead of paying for washes. The Journal cited a driver in Orange, Texas, who paid $944.44 to fill his 18-wheeler, compared to around $500 a year ago. The Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association warns that more small operators will file for bankruptcy if fuel prices remain high. Diesel prices have surged following disruptions to global oil trade caused by President Donald Trump's war against Iran, which has been described as deeply unpopular. item.title: HeyDude Faces Backlash for Collaborating with University of Florida Fraternity Amid Sexual Cyberharassment Allegations
item.description: A popular footwear brand, HeyDude, has faced significant backlash after posting a collaborative Instagram ad with the University of Florida's Theta Chi fraternity. The post, which featured fraternity members wearing the brand's 'Wally' loafer shoes, sparked controversy due to recent allegations against two former fraternity members, Kamran Ahmed and Brendan Pitfield, who are accused of disseminating nonconsensual intimate images of a fellow student, Maddie Kowalski. The Gainesville Police Department affidavit states that the posts, made using anonymous burner accounts, caused Kowalski 'widespread public humiliation and significant emotional distress.' Ahmed and Pitfield are charged with sexual cyberharassment, a first-degree misdemeanor punishable by up to a year in jail and a $1,000 fine. Kowalski is also suing them for financial damages. item.title: National Science Foundation Withheld $1.4 Billion in Congressional Research Funding
item.description:
The National Science Foundation withheld $1.4 billion in research funding that Congress had authorized during the past year, according to internal data reviewed by The New York Times. The amount represents roughly one-fifth of the agency’s primary research budget and signals a significant shift in how federal science funds are being managed.
The decision came as the Trump administration sought greater control over federal research priorities. Administration officials reportedly wanted to redirect some of the money toward a narrower group of priorities, including artificial intelligence and quantum computing. The move followed repeated efforts by the White House to reduce or reshape funding for major scientific agencies, proposals that lawmakers from both parties have generally opposed.

item.description: President Donald Trump expressed nostalgia for his life before entering politics during a rally in Vandalia, Ohio, on October 3, 2026. Speaking to attendees, Trump lamented the loss of his 'simple life,' stating he 'didn't have to be here on Saturday night going like this, working my a-- off in front of you people!' He added that he 'could have been home, I could have been in Monte Carlo, I could have been wherever the hell I wanted to be!' Trump has made similar remarks for over a decade, including during the 2016 presidential election and the recent RNC midterm convention in Texas. Trump acknowledged his desire to continue his presidency, saying he 'would love to do the four-more-years thing,' before shifting focus to criticize the media. item.description: President Donald Trump made a statement at a rally in Vandalia, Ohio on October 3, 2026, where he claimed he had 'among the highest IQs anywhere in the world' after noticing that a proposed $1,775 payment to U.S. service members was one dollar short of $1,776, a reference to the year of American independence.
